text_fidelity_a: Gorilla Carts 200 Pound Capacity Foldable Heavy Duty Poly Fishing and Marine Outdoor Sporting Goods Utility Cart with Rod Holders and Bait Tray, Gray I think overall it's a pretty nice cart.  Only a few things bother me.  Firstly, the included fillet table doesnt stay perfectly horizontal and it slants downwards, causing things to fall off very easily and making it useless.  I have to cut things on top of my cooler now.  Secondly, when I put my surf rods on the rod holders, the handles are way too long and it would drag against the floor.  Not much of a problem when you put the rods towards the front and you lift the cart to move it, but still, I wish the rod holders would sit a little higher.  On the beach (carrying a lot of items), I was able to drag the cart, but it was a lot of work dragging it.  I wish the tires were better (the fat poly type) and I wish there was actually 4 wheels to better distribute the weight (although I dont know if 4 wheels are better in the sand).  I think this cart would work great on a pier, but I think theres better, cheaper, and easier to transport options out there for pier use, such as those carts that easily fold up that you buy at costco or dicks sporting goods for about $40.  I dont know, maybe next time, I'll leave my rotomolded cooler in my car and I'll haul a soft cooler to hold fish temporarily, I'll see if itll make a significant difference in effort to haul this cart across the sand.

text_fidelity_a:
Continental Hometrainer Folding Tire I spent too much time reading about trainer tires and couldn't get any solid sense of a consensus, even an internet consensus. The best I was able to do was notice that people endorsing this tire gave cogent arguments for why they liked it; so I figured at least good critical thought was filtering opinions on these.

My experience is that it works great on the trainer. I have no other trainer tire for comparison; but compared with a road tire (Specialized Turbo Pro) it is night and day better. It grips better (e.g. sprints), is quieter... I guess that's enough.

I did get a tire bead jack to install it, but after the valve failed on the antique tube I was using, I was able to get this tire re-seated with my fingers. So maybe just the first installation is hard?

If you are like I was, combing through endless, non-comparative reviews of trainer tires, STOP RIGHT NOW AND BUY THIS ONE. It works great. There may be one that is better by some criterion over a very long period of time, but there is nothing wrong with this tire. I can't imagine any improvement. It even costs less than a typical road tire.

More advice: I thought it was frivolous to assemble a wheel just for the trainer but now I regret not doing it sooner. They have very cheap, serviceable wheels - and great prices on better wheels - right here on Amazon. I recommend keeping a separate wheel for the trainer so there is no disincentive for switching back and forth between indoors/out - and maybe more importantly, no incentive for buying another bike.
text_fidelity_b: Continental Hometrainer Folding Tire

The shears are a great starter/smaller set, not flimsy like others I have found in other kits. The TQ is your standard CAT clone. With those clones I can get occlusion quickly and easily on both upper arm and thigh placement on large (250lb +) and smaller (95lb) sized people. The windless will hold up well, its is well made and strong. The compressed gauze is a great little addition to this bag as well. The Israeli bandage is well made, vacuum packed and does not need to be opened and "staged" like some that are sewen through. The tactical pen is very heavy and a nice rollerball style refil, the glass break on the back is very sharp and appears to be tool steel or high carbon.
I added about $15 worth of add-ons to make it complete Bleed/IFAK. A pair of chest seals, additional rolled gauze, some 4x4's, some tape and an "ouch pouch" consisting of some band-aids, sting pads, loperamide and Benadryl. Even with the added items, there is still room for more in the kit if needed. I did go through and vacuum seal all of the items I added other than the ouch pouch as I do in all my IFAKs I build for spaace and to keep things clean.
I noticed that I bought these when they were deeply discounted at $24 each, and if they drop down to that price again I will be buying more.

SEAL SwimSafe Monitor System with Swim Bands Let me first say. . . This is one incredible system. It really works. It’s very easy to set-up. There are four levels so depending upon if your child can swim a little. . a lot. . . or not at all. . . it will alert. There are other pool alarms on the market which will tell you when the pool has been disturbed, but this system goes far beyond that letting you know about each swimmer.

Note that the band is about 14 inches around on the inside. But there is an included “extender” which will make it about 18 inches. So it’s good with not only small kids, but older kids as well. .. and possibly some adults.

I do have one “issue”. . . and that’s the cost. This is the one-band listing. Extra bands cost about one hundred fifty bucks. But if you look, you will see that currently there is a listing for a two-band set, which is even less expensive than the one-band set. . . and you get two bands. There’s also a four-band set, which can save you some money if you need that many bands. I’m just saying to check all the listings before purchasing. You’ll want bands not only for your own kids, but any visiting kids as well. I really think this system is going to save a lot of lives. You just have to make sure you use it each time you’re around water. It won’t work. . if you don’t use it.
text_fidelity_b: SEAL SwimSafe Monitor System with Swim Bands

text_fidelity_a:
LeupoldRX-1200i Rangefinder Matte This range finder is excellent. Leupold has packed a lot of features into a range finder for under $200. I ranged on some known distances and it was right on as far as accuracy goes. I did not test it past 500 meters but im sure you could really push this one out and still have good accuracy. I like the automatic True Ballistic Range calculation--it really lends itself well to hunting with rifle or bow. I also use this range finder's LOS settings for photography-related hobbies. Knowing distances of natural objects in a scene can help with prime lens choice, etc. This range finder is useful everywhere. In addition to being an awesome range finder, it makes for a great monocular. I find myself using it a lot while hunting rather than pulling up big, heavy binoculars. The magnification and clarity of the optic is great--which is to be expected from leupold.

I really like the case that came with the range finder. It carries the unit very well and it also has a card spot for carrying a range card. It actually includes a range card and a micro fiber cloth for cleaning your optics. Last but not least, the unit came with a battery. It is nice being able to take this out of the box and immediately use it. I bought [[ASIN:B0057ILX8S these batteries]] to use in it after the original is dead. The original that came with the unit is an energizer brand.

Dimensions of the case and the range finder unit can be seen in the photos I have uploaded

Included:
-Range finder unit
-Micro Fiber cloth
-Range Reference Card
-Carrying case (unit pocket, range card slot)
-Manual

Pros:
*Extremely accurate ranging
*TBR calculations
*Bow, Rifle, and LOS options
*Small and light
*Waterproof

Cons:
*None

Additional Considerations:
Leupold makes very solid optic-related products. You cannot really go wrong with them. They do well by their customers from what I have experienced and observed.

Overall: 5/5 stars (>=.5 rounds up, <.5 rounds down) => 5 stars

If you have any further questions regarding the product in my review please leave a comment below and I will get back to you as soon as possible.
text_fidelity_b: LeupoldRX-1200i Rangefinder Matte

text_fidelity_a:
Elvira 32oz Large Water Bottle with Motivational Time Marker & Removable Strainer,Fast Flow BPA Free Non-Toxic for Fitness, Gym and Outdoor Sports For whatever reason, mine did not come with the strainer. If it did, I'd likely not have used it anyway, as I don't find a need to add fruit to my water. But since it was supposed to, I need to mention it. For some, it may be the very reason you select it. Product description states to contact them if there are any issues.

The bottle itself is solid. Holds a little over 32 ounces, has markings to help guide you in adequate water consumption, and the plastic is BPA free. I have other water bottle brand/style that I prefer-especially for carrying around with me, but this one has been good for use in the house through the day.

The bottle and lid is simple. The top screws on. There is a flip top with an opening approximately size of a quarter to drink from. If you want a larger opening, just unscrew the lid entirely. I prefer to do the latter to as it is easier for me to guzzle down some water that way. The wide open bottle is nice for cleaning purpose. And stuffing bottle with ice.

A good sized carry strap for convenience.

While the bottle cap feels secure, I am not inclined to toss this in a bag like my preferred water bottle. I am not too sure how well the flip top would stay on. I could be wrong, but I don't want to risk it. For me, this is strictly for around the house use. That being said..

I don't have too much trouble getting my water intake. I'm not on a diet, I have never noticed that drinking water helps with any of that, but I do prefer to stay hydrated and also simply enjoy plain cold water. Of all the bad choices I make for myself, I tend to always choose water to drink. I am a champ with getting my water in all summer, but I do slow up a bit come winter. I keep a 32 ounce bottle on me all day, and I even have another one at my bedside. This bottle is also 32 ounces (actually a little more, since the 32 ounce line is a few inches from top). The difference between my other bottles and this one, is that there is a little motivating factor through the use of time stamped on the bottle. The idea is to fill the bottle twice to get the recommended water intake. I thought if anything, this is what might remind me to keep drinking my water as we head into winter months. I wasn't sure if I was going to pay much attention to it enough to help me, but I find that the first thing I do in the morning is to fill my bottle to the top. I usually guzzle down 16 ounces almost immediately, After that, it is just a matter of looking at my bottle through the day, paying attention to the time, and making a point to take a good long drink. Refill and repeat. A simple, handy thing. My preferred bottles don't have that :)

And so, I am sold on the effectiveness of the time stamp. A little thing, but it does help. I don't need motivational quotes, just the easy at a glance view of my water level and the time. Good for me!

So I see no reason not to be happy with this bottle- unless you don't get the filter like me. . It is reasonably priced, good sized capacity that is easy to work with (basically drain and fill twice!). Cap off makes it easy to drink down a bunch of water, or just flip the cap to take swigs as needed. If you find yourself not drinking enough at once, I recommend drinking from wider opening.

Bottle is wide, may or may not fit in your vehicle cup holder, and as for carrying around casually in a bag.. still not sure how secure it is. It isn't subpar, just be mindful. Even with that consideration I recommend it, and consider it a 4.5-5 star product (if stays under $15)
text_fidelity_b: Elvira 32oz Large Water Bottle with Motivational Time Marker & Removable Strainer,Fast Flow BPA Free Non-Toxic for Fitness, Gym and Outdoor Sports

MASXODRK Universal Scooter Bag,Waterproof and Stable Handlebar Bag for Scooter/EBike/Motorcycle/Bicycle,Large Capacity&Portable EVA Scooter Accessories Storage Bag for Charger,Repair Tools&Phone I fully admit, we got this MASXODRK Scooter Bag, Large Capacity Waterproof Electric Scooter Storage Bag for our two unknown/lesser known brand eScooters not knowing if we had a chance for it to fit. It is not one of the ones listed on the product page, so... in the end, it has worked out great on both our eScooters, so we are happy to have it.

This MASXODRK Scooter Bag, Large Capacity Waterproof Electric Scooter Storage Bag has two straps at the top to go on the handlebars, two on the back to wrap and hold it to the upright stick of the eScooter. But would there be enough room between/around/next too the break and accelerator? For both of ours, yes. They fit slightly differently, but yes, we got them on there, no problem. The straps on the back - one over the other - holds the bag to the stick perfectly. The top ones come with such a long piece of material, you have various options on length down the front stick - we can actually do it at varying heights and simply wrap the remaining material. The ones on the back are a little more limited, but not so much that we could not also adjust - here it was how tight to make it against the stick, and this varied by how high or low we did the top one. In other words, there is enough material on the top two straps that it allowed us to adjust the placement of the bag on the two different eScooters, and on each eScooter itself, for more overall options.

The bag is a good size. We can get both wallets, a phone or two, keys, all in there. The velcro holds it strong enough. And we are good to go. We do NOT ride in any weather, so no idea how it would handle rain - but we never want to find out. We THINK it would be okay and keep stuff good. There is a solid, type material for the shell, cloth for the edges, all SHOULD hold back the rain - but that cloth COULD potentially get soaked and leaked. But our understanding of eScooters - you'd have a bigger problem with the scooter getting wet first.

In the end we are thrilled with this MASXODRK Scooter Bag, Large Capacity Waterproof Electric Scooter Storage Bag and while we are using it on our eScooters, we feel it would go on a bike or other item as well, depending on the design of course, but opens more options for using it. We're thrilled.

GTGlobal Multifunctional Beach Blanket/ Picnic Mat with Carrying Pouch 7 X 5 Feet, Waterproof Tarp, Extra Large Perfect for Beach Party/ Outdoors/ Camping/ Hiking - Green Measuring 7'x5', the GT Global Beach Blanket is a nice size for a picnic lunch or to spread out on the beach for sunbathing. As others have previously noted, this "blanket" is a lightweight, thin, smooth nylon-like material with grommets around the sides, so it's more of a light tarp rather than a blanket, but that's not at all bad. This material stays cool to the touch so it would be a real relief to sunbathe on this rather than my towel which transfers heat directly to me when laying on it.

Sand doesn't stick to this material and water beads up and rolls right off it, so you could use this as a protective layer to keep your beach towels or blanket clean. Being very light, it's easy for the breeze to catch it and sail it away, so it has grommets strategically positioned around the sides which would allow it to be staked down. (Stakes not included). It could also make a handy sunshade if you had someplace to secure it from and some line.

It comes in a nylon carry case that's very tight so it's a bit of an effort to remove it. When you're done using it the bag would be handy to store it in again, but it's so tight that I was unable to place it back in. The manufacturer really needs to make the carry bag large enough that people could use it without struggling.

Even without going back into the bag though, this tarp folds and rolls up into a small bundle that would be easy to take along to the beach, waterpark, on camping trips, to stick in a backpack for trekking, or to stow on a boat. Besides using it for picnics or at the beach, this tarp would be very useful to have along when camping to provide a dry place to sit or to cover food stores or gear. Backpackers would find it useful to provide a safe dry seating area, to hang up by the grommets to get out of sudden downpours, and even as something to sleep on at night in a pinch. Boaters could find this tarp useful in many of the same ways and more, so this tarp has uses that go way beyond "beach blanket", and for those reasons I like it.

I'm giving it four stars rather than five because it's impossible to return the tarp to the carry bag once it's out of it, and it needs to come with stakes to hold it down in sand to be ready to use. Promotional discount received for evaluation and review purposes.
text_fidelity_b: GTGlobal Multifunctional Beach Blanket/ Picnic Mat with Carrying Pouch 7 X 5 Feet, Waterproof Tarp, Extra Large Perfect for Beach Party/ Outdoors/ Camping/ Hiking - Green

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Inspire 2 Health & Fitness Tracker with a Free 1-Year Fitbit Premium Trial, 24/7 Heart Rate, Black/Rose, One Size (S & L Bands Included) I purchased this model/version because my Charge 4 stopped working after only 2 years of use. The Inspire 2 is a smaller display and, depending on the templates you download on the app, can have more details showing on the home screen. There are a few things that I would complain about but are not major issues: first, there are 2 touch-sensitive nodes on the sides that seem to go off when my wrists are bent back and this happens very often which makes me think the notifications have gone off; the second is that I can’t adjust the vibration intensity on the watch so I miss phone calls and messages many times.

This is still a great buy if you only need the basics. All the features for heart rate, steps, and (this one shows) activity time are what you’re looking for when buying a watch like this.

Fitbit Charge 4 vs Inspire 2: What's the difference?
The Inspire 2 has a plastic body so it's a little cheaper in its appearance compared to the Charge 4. It also has a smaller touchscreen display than the Charge and it has a physical button on the side, making for a less streamlined design than the other two models.

Ultimately, it’s lightweight, compact, and doesn’t use up excessive power like other smartwatches on the market. It also charges pretty fast (20-30 minutes for a full charge) and it takes about 4-5 days to run out of power (2 days for smartwatches). I would definitely recommend that someone to buy it for fitness purposes.

Overall, an economical watch that does the job.

Cons: Fitbits stop working after a couple of years for no reason. This is my 4th one in the last 6 years.

This thing easily popped off and in spite of her dainty skills at repairing such tiny things, cannot get it back on. That’s a minus for us.

But as a tool, it’s great. So if they can fix that flaw in how the port cover is attached, we’d be happy to give it a 5.

It arrived in a nice box (for yourself or a gift) in 3 parts: light, clamp, and charger. She charged right away - after as she pushed the piece in it popped off - and we put it on. She severely broke her foot a couple weeks ago and gets around for the next 3 months on a scooter. But she wants to be able to see at night if she’s moving through the house, or if we are outside, so we thought a bike light might work. It’s perfect for that. It fits on the handles of her scooter as easily as a bike - and we plan on switching it to a bike when she’s recovered. In the mean time, the 3 levels of light mean she can see safely in the house without being disruptive, and she can see safely outside moving to the car or around our home. It’s really easy to clamp and remove - she takes it off when we are in the car so it won’t get broken off. And she can easily pop it back on.

Overall this is a great light and minus the flaw with the port cover, we are really happy with it. That we cannot overlook, however, because there is little doubt that in 12+ weeks on the scooter and future use on the bike, covering the port hole would be a safety issue (rain). text_fidelity_a:
Leslie Sansone: Walk Away the Pounds for Abs: 3 Miles VHS This was my first-ever Leslie Sansone video, and I was surprised by how tough it was, especially given that I already exercise regularly and have even started a running program in the past month. Leslie uses four basic moves--march, side step, front kick, and knee lift--but varies the speed and execution of each movement to change the intensity. In addition, this workout uses Leslie's special weight belt for upper body toning work; I don't own the belt, so I substituted light (3 lb.) hand weights throughout the workout.

The workout begins with Leslie introducing the four basic moves, and in the warm-up phase, she gradually picks up the pace until you are moving along at a fairly good clip. At this point (about 10 minutes into the workout), she introduces use of the belt or weights for some basic upper body exercises, including overhead press and flies. For the middle part of the workout, or Mile 2, the weights are not used, as the pace increases considerably. Although the movements stayed the same, I sometimes found it a bit difficult to keep up with Leslie's quick movements. However, Leslie is extremely encouraging, frequently saying that it's okay to go at your own pace and not to follow her form exactly. For the first half of the last mile, the belt or weights are again used, repeating many of the previous exercises. The pace then slows down a bit to start bringing your heart rate back to normal, and finally, the last 2 minutes of the workout consists of cool-down stretches for a total of 44 minutes.

The only problem I had with this workout is the title, as I think it would have more appropriately been named WATP for Upper Body rather than Abs. Leslie does provide frequent reminders to concentrate on your abs and some of the moves (especially the knee lifts) do work the abdominal area, but the toning segments were more focused on the upper body in general. Overall, however, I found this to be an excellent cardio workout, and although the moves are repetitive, the time really does fly by. It is probably most appropriate for intermediate exercisers, but experienced beginners could manage by moving at a slower pace and skipping the weights.
text_fidelity_b: Leslie Sansone: Walk Away the Pounds for Abs: 3 Miles VHS

text_fidelity_a:
CamelBak Chute Mag Vacuum Insulated I love to have water with me. The problem is that the containers either are too hard to get into especially when I only have one hand available, or they spill on me, or the caps flap back onto my face making me dribble water all over. Let's see how this container performed.

WHAT IS THIS BOTTLE LIKE?
This bottle is thick. It is stainless steel with a painted black bottom on it. It has a wide opening of about 2 1/4 inches wide. It is double walled and stainless steel inside too. The top is thick plastic. It has a handle built into it, and it screws onto the bottom nicely. The cap of the bottle screws on with inside threads (not outside) and it snaps back so that a magnet holds the cap against the side of the top so it stays out of the way when drinking.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
This container is amazing. I have put cold water in the bottle with no ice and after about four hours in close to 100 degrees the water was still cool. I have put ice in this container and the water has stayed cold for two days- although it was not near 100 degrees all of that time.

The handle is easy to carry, and the cap stays out of the way perfectly. This is easy to drink from and I am thriled that it also fits into my car cup holders without tipping over. That may not be the case with every car, but with mine it is.

EASY TO CLEAN
The opening is large enough to get a good bottle brush in there to clean it with. It is wider than many other containers I have used.

ANY PROBLEMS?
The only thing I am not fond of is the plastic piece that folds to hold the cap onto the container. It seems like a flimsy connection of plastic and I can see it breaking down quickly. I will update my review should that happen.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a nice sturdy container to keep liquids cold for at least a day or more, this is a wonderful purchase. It is easy to carry, great to drink from and has a large enough hole to make it easy to clean too.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS! This is my favorite container of this type so far.
text_fidelity_b: CamelBak Chute Mag Vacuum Insulated

Meditation bench, Seiza Bench,It's Adjustable, Portable,Lightweight and Durable I'm over 60, and wanted to learn to sit seiza again; however sharp pains in my calfs and ankles made it difficult to maintain. I figured I could work up to it with this little bench, and it's doing the trick!! I gradually lowered the height to the lowest level...then I took a 7/8" diameter dowel and some scrap wood, and made a substitute "T" to fit under the seat. As my comfort with a height increases, I take the dowel and saw off about 1/4" at a time to reduce the height a bit. I'm finally able to sit seiza, even without the bench, without serious pain; I'll continue to lower the height and practice daily until I don't need the bench at all, but in the meantime, it makes sitting seiza for extended periods much more comfortable.

As others have noted, the bench has little padding (just a thin layer of dense foam), so this may not be comfortable if you're carrying much excess weight, since that would increase the pressure on your thighs. Renegade GK Fury Goalie Gloves with Microbe-Guard (Sizes 6-11, 7 Styles, Level 4) Pro-Tek Fingersaves & 4+3MM Giga Grip | High Performance Pro-Level Goalkeeper Glove | Based in The USA This is an absolutely fantastic keeper glove with just one nuance with the right thumb fingersave.

The gloves are nice and cool with a mesh that lets the hand breathe on the back. The grip is great even though it is smooth! The palms are solid and feel like a mix of latex and neoprene and seem to breathe so my palms don't get as sweaty as other gloves. The latex is a bit soft and after a half-dozen practices with 4-5x the shots I would have in a game, it hasn't disappointed. However, there are some chunks that are missing. I change gloves nearly every season or two. There is a latex wraparound for the thumb that keeps the grip throughout the throw to my teammates. It's like I am getting an extra yard or two and can put a little spin on the ball if I like.

The hard ball comes in up high like a hornet and it's easy to swat down. I just don't feel the sting like some other, thinner, gloves have. Punching the ball is still possible with the fingersave *but* I rarely punch the ball.

The only thing I dislike is how they have the fingersave build into the thumb. It presses in on the top and side of the nail bed and is uncomfortable. I haven't found a way to push it down 1/2 inch and certainly can't change the angle. The left glove fits like, well, a glove and I barely notice the same thing but still notice it. Instead of a hard edge they might need to change the layout of the fingersave.

Normally I wear an Adidas or Reusch and this may be pushing Reusch out and into my new favorite. If I can figure a way out to warm up and melt the thumb fingersave to put a little curve into it, this would be the perfect glove.

I do not wash my gloves so haven't had any issues with the dye. I will gently wipe down the latex and the back of the glove unless the glove gets muddy. There are some renewal products that bring the tackiness back to the latex but I have not tried them with this glove.
text_fidelity_b: Renegade GK Fury Goalie Gloves with Microbe-Guard (Sizes 6-11, 7 Styles, Level 4) Pro-Tek Fingersaves & 4+3MM Giga Grip | High Performance Pro-Level Goalkeeper Glove | Based in The USA

Aoneky Adjustable Kids Jump Rope with Counter and Comfortable Handles This jump rope is well made with very comfortable handles. The foam grips are just the right size. The rope itself is easily adjustable and LONG. I'm 4'11" tall, and I had to take it up a lot to get it to a length that was right for me. Because I won't be sharing this with anyone else, I cut some of the extra length off, but if you're sharing with someone tall, you might not want to do that.

The counter issue that several people have mentioned concerned me at first, too, but then I read that you MUST have the counter in your right hand. If you don't, the rope will be turning in the wrong direction so of course it's not going to count. Once I made sure the counter was in my right hand, I found the counter to be accurate and reliable.

I would have given this five stars, but five stars means "I love it" and I can't say I love it. This is not because the product doesn't deserve the high rating; it's because I find I really don't love jumping rope with a lighter weight jump rope. I loved it when I was a kid and we were literally jumping ropes on the playground with those heavy ropes that thwacked when they hit the ground and gave a pleasurable sensation on the upswing. There's no way to make a lightweight jump rope that has that kind of tactile feedback, and that's what I always loved about jumping rope.
text_fidelity_b: Aoneky Adjustable Kids Jump Rope with Counter and Comfortable Handles

ARCEE Headlamp & Camping Lantern for Kids, Lightweight Portable Outdoor Indoor Tent Lamp for Children, Lanterns for Emergency, Hurricane, Power Outage, Nightlight for Kids’ Room Geared toward kids, yet anyone can benefit from it. Both the lantern and the headlamp come with preinstalled AA batteries, and CR2032 respectively. There is a spot in the description where it says "not included" but they are, and another that said they are. They are, can confirm. Just pull the little battery saver tab to activate. To access the battery compartment, you will need a tiny Phillips head screwdriver. Flat works too.

Both items are well made and durable feeling. I got that impression while unboxing. It just has a good feel, not cheap feeling. My video and pics are taken in a small dark storage room. Not actually producing colors.

The HEAD LAMP band is stretchy and adjustable. I was able to slide it onto y large 23.75" head. It is not something all that practical--no way to direct the light like one would with an adult sized head lamp but it is still useful. Good way to keep track of kid in darkness (camping, Halloween, emergency). It imparts a decent amount of direct light. I would even keep this in my car as a little emergency light. I could probably use this as a reading light if I wore it on my neck. Maybe.

TO OPERATE: press yellow button on top. THIS could be tricky for some kids and adults. As the pressure point location is directly in the convex center. Cant just press any spot on the yellow surface. Must be directly between eyes. Once that is figured out, then it is super easy.

The LANTERN is lightweight, yet robust feeling. Has TWO light options: top flashlight, forward direction. OR a diffuse lower lantern light. I think it lights up well enough for the space around. I am not sure why we would need to give a kid a spotlight (I just imagine little kiddos trying to blind others, This wont do that). This light is perfectly fine for them--in a tent, around their little area in an emergency, as their own bed side flashlight or night light of the sorts. I would use this myself in car, for sitting outside in evening, for light glow while walking around with dogs, or on my own, etc. I carry strong mag lights, but I find this little pack useful. Nice handle. Can be popped off if need be. Good base- wont easily tip over. Can take a drop to the ground, I think. Could hook this to a backpack and have lead adult or older kiddo to light up a path.

TO OPERATE: very easy, very intuitive, easy to press single button. Press to turn on upper flashlight, press again to switch it to the lantern. Another press simply turns it off.

I see they have an owl option and I love owls. My only choice was a frog. Frogs are cool, but owls are my love. I like this lantern enough to want to buy the owl for myself. I plan to keep the headlamp in my bag, and the lantern will just set out. I figured if the power goes out, it can't hurt to have extra options that don't require me to hold onto it. I can keep this on one of my end tables, and just press the button. Then I can use it to go get other supplies and such. Will make for a good glow, enough to light up area enough to be comfortable to maneuver.

----->>>>>>>In summary: This is a great little set. Fun looking, nice lights, COMES WITH BATTERIES INSTALLED, stretchy headband not limited to child use, good material, good feel, and is just refreshingly NICE product. Not cruddy feeling or looking. I do not rate on price, but I thought the full price reasonable. I bought the second one on sale (Prime Day), which was even better!

I recommend this for kids, for adults who still enjoy kid like stuff, for gift giving (I'll for practical gifts, and for a kid this would be fun and practical). They did well with including pre-installed batteries (just pull-out battery saver tag--if it doesn't fully come out, you will need to go in and take it out).
text_fidelity_b: ARCEE Headlamp & Camping Lantern for Kids, Lightweight Portable Outdoor Indoor Tent Lamp for Children, Lanterns for Emergency, Hurricane, Power Outage, Nightlight for Kids’ Room

CAP Barbell Premium Bumper Plate Set These bumper plates are great for being able to begin the deadlift. It is useful for people who want to begin the deadlift at 55 or 64 pounds (depending on the weight of your bar). This is perfect for people with past injury, people who want to perfect form, or just someone who likes to take things easy at first.

The inside of the 2 inch hole in the center is steel lined so it is nice and durable and solid on the bar. The actual plastic/rubber part of the disc that provides the bulk of the weight is semi flexible which will save the floor from skuffs. Just be aware if you want to load other metal weights onto the bar these bumper plates will flex eventually. So if you want to add 25 or 35's on the sides you will need to add more bumpers to compensate if you start adding a lot of weight. Obviously when you progress to a 135+ weight just find a set of 45lbs bumper plates which will be thicker.

These weights had a slight smell to them and an oily residue on the rubber part of the plate. While annoying at first it goes away relatively quickly.

The dimensions of this plate are standard olympic size in all aspects. The plate is around 1 inch wide. All of these dimensions can be viewed in the photos I have uploaded to the review.

This is a set of TWO (2) plates.

Pros:
*Standard Olympic 2 inch bar plate
*Allows for beginners to start light on the deadlift.

Cons:
*Oily and smelly residue on plate out of the box(- 1/2 a star)

Coleman Big Basin Cold-Weather Sleeping Bag, 15°F Big & Tall Camping Sleeping Bag for Adults, Adjustable Hood and Fleece-Lined Footbox for Warmth and Ventilation, Fits Adults up to 6ft 6in Tall I was an Eagle Scout and we've used these bags a few times in temps down to freezing, and they work great if you get a fleece bag liner and put it in there. We were really nice and toasty warm.

PROS:
- HUGE - really really big. I'm 6ft and not small, and there's loads of extra room. If you don't like being cramped, look no further.
- WARM - It's actually pretty darn warm on it's own.
- GOOD ZIPPERS - they're on the left if you're laying in the bag, and they work well without getting caught a lot.
- TWO ZIPPERS - One down the side and one on the bottom. Why is this good? Zippers tend to have issues going around corners, and this seems to help.
- ZIPPER DRAFT TUBE - Huh? They made an extra...insulated tube of fabric next to the zippers running lengthwise that helps keep air out. And it's made of tougher material almost like a backpack which means...drum roll...the zipper finally doesn't get caught on the bag itself!!!
- GOOD HOOD - The hood is really nice and roomy, like put a full size pillow in it roomy. If you sinch it up with the draw string you can have a face-size opening.
- FLEECE FOOT - the inside bottom foot and a half has an extra layer of warm fleece.
- BURROW - I like to kind of burrow down in a sleeping bag and there's so much room you can bend your legs, sleep on your side, have your arm curled under your head, and there's just so much room. I can put my fee at the very bottom and have the opening above my head.
- LOOKS COOL - I know, it's a sleeping bag and how cool do you expect it to look, really? But it really does look pretty cool.

CONS:
- BIG - We put them in stuff sacks that sinch down and they're still pretty big bags.
- NOT FOR BACKPACKING - like everyone says.

HOW TO SLEEP WARMER:
- Put an inexpensive and washable fleece liner inside the bag. There's plenty of room. It adds to the warmth significantly.
- Change your clothes before you sleep. During the day your clothes get moisture from your own body heat. Change before you sleep and not only will you be warmer, having clean clothes inside the bag makes it stay cleaner.
- Don't over-dress. Start off in like shorts and a t-shirt, no socks, and you'll be warm without sweating. If you start off too warm, you'll build up heat, sweat, and then be colder.
- Put your extra layers down in the foot. Got a sweatshirt you'll probably wear in the morning? Shove it down in the foot. There's room, and it'll be warm when you're ready for it in the morning.
- Wear a beanie, helps with heat loss on your head if you stick your head out for fresh air.

FLEECE LINER:
We used something like this (though not this exact one) and it gets even warmer.
https://www.amazon.com/Stansport-Fleece-Sleeping-Bag-Red/dp/B002YXITMW/ref=sr_1_7?dchild=1&keywords=fleece+sleeping+bag+liner&qid=1592870476&sr=8-7

STUFF SACK:
We used a compression stuff sack like this and were able to fit the sleeping bag and the fleece liner in it together.
https://www.amazon.com/Lewis-N-Clark-Compression-Drawstring/dp/B079JRVVD1/ref=sr_1_4?dchild=1&keywords=lewis+n.+clark+compression+sack&qid=1592870350&sr=8-4
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Big Basin Cold-Weather Sleeping Bag, 15°F Big & Tall Camping Sleeping Bag for Adults, Adjustable Hood and Fleece-Lined Footbox for Warmth and Ventilation, Fits Adults up to 6ft 6in Tall

text_fidelity_a:
Gaiam Total Body Balance Ball Kit - Includes Anti-Burst Stability Exercise Yoga Ball, Air Pump, Workout Program For sitting long periods of time on the ball, going a size up is a good idea, but I have found that you want to stick with your size for the stretches and workouts to get the most out of them. For instance, I am 5'4" or 5'5" and definitely need to go back and buy the smaller ball for the workouts. But I prefer either the 65" or the 75" for sitting for any period of time. Getting two sizes is a really worthwhile investment, imo. I always sit on a ball or on a balance cushion (when not in a recliner) b/c of hip and back issues, and it makes SUCH a difference. [[UPDATE: the 55" is way too small for me. It seems what I'd really need are two 65" w/ one of them far less inflated for doing the workout... sigh]]

I had problems w/ the DVD from the go--it was a mess even though it wasn't scratched. The part I could see I really liked, but with medical disabilities, it was a little too hard on my body anyhow (do not underestimate the after-effects of swinging a ball full of air over your head--lol--amazing workout!). When I contacted Gaiam about the DVD, they sent me a replacement. Happily, it was different one that was more suited to my health, a beginner's workout done by a blonde woman named Suzanne. It consists of 45 minutes of mostly stretches. I've done it every day for a week, and my chiropractor cannot believe the difference in my spinal health and other parts of my body as well--even my g.i. So score for Gaiam as a company and for their videos! It may seem like a long time to just stretch (w/ a modicum of strength and toning), but it is proving to be so worth it.

As for the videos that come with this ball, they consist of far less stretching and more aerobic strengthening from what I can tell. I really like the woman who leads them.

I had problems getting any of the three plugs that came with the ball into the ball. The hole really was not shaped properly. I solved this by substituting the somewhat smaller plug from my balance cushion until I had stretched the hole out sufficiently. I realize, however, that not all of you will have another plug lying around and so thought I should mention that. Probably if you jammed the plug as far as it would go and sat on the ball for a few days w/o exercising, it would stretch out and go into the hole.
text_fidelity_b: Gaiam Total Body Balance Ball Kit - Includes Anti-Burst Stability Exercise Yoga Ball, Air Pump, Workout Program

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge 2 Heart Rate + Fitness Wristband, Teal, Small (US Version) The device works fine. I don't think the step count is particularly accurate, as it seems to be based on hand motion as much as anything else (as I really racked up the mileage while chopping vegetables), but it's definitely in the ballpark and gives you a pretty good idea of your level of activity. I really like the e-mail and text alerts.

What I don't like: THE BAND. I purchased this device in December 2016 and didn't get around to wearing it until January 2017. It is now March. The band has broken TWICE -- it comes detached on the buckle side, where the band attaches to the device. Once it becomes detached, it will never stay secure again. Although I can slide it back together, it easily comes off when I'm pulling off a coat or a sweater. I can understand this happening once, but TWICE??? Never had this problem with my Charge.

Fortunately, FITBIT customer service is very helpful. They have sent replacement bands at no charge, which I truly appreciate. However, I would much prefer the device just stayed in one piece and I didn't have to mess with the replacement band over and over. I've tried to figure out if I'm doing something wrong -- but the instructions for replacing the bands are pretty straight-forward, so I'm not sure how you'd go wrong.

Overall, I like the functionality of the device but sure wish the band would stop breaking!
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge 2 Heart Rate + Fitness Wristband, Teal, Small (US Version)

text_fidelity_a:
Old Timer Generational USA Series Traditional Fixed and Folding Knives with 1095 HC Stainless Steel Blades, Sawcut Bone Handles, and Made in USA for Hunting, Skinning, EDC, Field Dressing, and Outdoor I have a pocket knife in my pocket at all times and I have found having one on me is almost always useful. I had not heard of Old Timer until recently, but their knives look nice and I thought I would give them a chance. So far I am very pleased with this particular knife.

This is a no-frills knife that doesn't try to get too fancy. The blades have to be pulled open manually without a spring assist, and it does not have some of the things that other knives frequently have such as a corkscrew, screwdriver and other integrated emergency tools. Instead it has three blades - nothing more. Each blade is different and has different uses, though the thought that comes to mind when I look at the knife as a whole is whittling and carving.

The blades are tight and do not wobble. That's a good thing and says that the knife as a whole is assembled well. The blades feel solid and secure when opened.

I love the bone handle. It feels good in the hand and it looks retro which is a good thing. The texture makes it easy to maintain a grip, even when hands are just a little wet.

This is a smallish knife, so it will fit in your pocket and not take up lots of room. text_fidelity_a:
Wilson Ultra Men's Right-Hand Golf Package Set Includes Irons, Woods, a Putter and a Stand Bag OK, first let me say that I am a beginner golfer (male, 5'11" and 210lb. ) and to clear up some other questions from previous posts, this is what is included:

1-Wood (Driver)
4-Hybrid
FW-Fairway Wood
5,6,7,8,9-Irons
PW-Pitching Wedge
Putter

Now for the review.

At the moment my favorite clubs in this set is the putter, PW, 5-iron and FW. Maybe those are my favorite because I have the most consistent results with them. Now to the point, the FW is the most forgiving wood I have ever used. The Putter, well I loved it the moment I was able to use it on the green... I look forward to getting to the green just so I can pull this baby out. Love the way it taps and it balances GREAT!!! This is not your typical putter. You will love the way it feels when it hits the ball. Trust me on this one. The PW performs very well. When I'm not using my 5-iron I go straight for the Pitching Wedge (but that could be that I am still learning how to position myself for the other irons).

The bag the clubs came in are already setting up the standards for what my future bag should have. The Driver, 4H and FW all had covers for them. The bag has a towel ring and plenty of storage space. I like the tee holster on the side of the bag as well as it is convenient. Additionally, the Bag Stand is activated when you tilt the bag forward...Very Nice...

I can see myself using this set of clubs for a good while. Today I played on the course with 3 of my buddies and all of them have been playing for years and have commented on how much better I am playing with these clubs than the rental sets. And for the price I paid for it I don't think I could have done better. I am happy with this set of clubs and its making my golf learning experience all the more enjoyable.

Thanks to Wilson for manufacturing such a great beginner (to intermediate maybe) set of clubs. The image is accurate for this set of clubs, but unfortunately they don't show all the clubs in the set. But you can Google another site for these same exact clubs and they have more images that you can check out.

Kudos to Amazon for shipping the product fast. I only requested standard delivery and my clubs arrived the next day!!! But that could be since it was shipped out of Pennsylvania to Washington DC. So its not that far away. It was shipped in the original Wilson box. Everything in the package was wrapped and protected during shipment.

John
text_fidelity_b: Wilson Ultra Men's Right-Hand Golf Package Set Includes Irons, Woods, a Putter and a Stand Bag

text_fidelity_a: Shimano PD-MX80 Platform Pedals I just recently discovered MTB and having a blast. Straight out of the gate I went ahead and converted to SPD but found I was having trouble. After doing a little research I found that most people were recommending platform pedals when first starting out on the mountain bike. So, a little research later and I found these Saint pedals by Shimano. It took a while to get used to not being securely attached to the bike (feet were bouncing off on rough terrain) but once I got the hang of being on a platform things improved quickly. I am far from being an expert rider but the Saints have certainly helped to improve my skills and my confidence as well. Along the way I have whacked some rocks very hard on multiple occasions but the Saints have just shrugged that off and kept right on going. I would also recommend, as others have, that you remove the washers from between the studs and the pedal and add the additional studs. If you're looking for some affordable, rugged platforms look no further.
text_fidelity_b: Shimano PD-MX80 Platform Pedals

The only compromise is tilting the desk all the way toward you, which makes it even more painful on your wrists and arms. Getting on or off the bike is very tricky - the handlebars are right there, so I kept banging my leg, it was very awkward. In fact that's how the entire structure is, very awkward, clunky, non-ergonomic, and tough to work with. Also, it is quite heavy, so folding it would still be hard to do even if it wasn't off center, It's not an easy task.

text_fidelity_a:
Osprey Stratos 50 Men's Backpacking Backpack There is a reason why Osprey's are one of the best selling packs on the market today. They combine great features, comfort, durability, and usefulness into one package. It has a 50L capacity.

First off, if you haven't had a new pack in a while, stop and get a new one. My old pack was one from the 90s, and though it served me well for many day hikes and overnighters, it was time to move up. And a step up it is.

First off the pack is light. New materials make this a very light pack. Also, the straps are highly adjustable for various sized people, so whether you are 5'6" or 6'2" you'll be able to find a comfortable fit for you. Another important thing is the fully padded shoulder and hip straps, which makes carrying heavy loads bearable and comfortable. The rig and internal frame is rigid, but not too heavy while not sacrificing comfort and adjust-ability.

Another aspect of this pack that is so great is how it carrys the load. Previous packs carried the load directly on your back, with much of the weight on the shoulders. This distributes the weight with more on your hips, saving your shoulders. It also keeps the pack a bit off your back. At first it feels a bit weird, as the center of gravity and weight distribution is a bit different that I was used to, but after a few miles I hardly felt I was carrying anything at all! Also, with the ventilated back, it keeps your back from rubbing against the pack and sweating so much.

There are pockets galore, including some nice zippered pouches on the hips, I use for my GPS, chapstick, etc. Mesh side pockets are good for medium sized water bottles, or whatever you want to put in there, snacks, flashlight, etc. Back pocket good sized as well.

The top flap is large and can hold a lot of stuff, and has a retainer for your keys. It can also be detached completely.

Top loading is a cinch, as it has multiple straps for tightening or loosening the pack to accommodate larger or smaller packouts. The large inside pocket can also be accessed by side zippers.

Inside the pack there is a pocket for your hydration system, that can feed up through the top of the pack and attaching to one of your shoulder straps.

The bottom of the pack features a tent/sleeping back compartment that can be accessed by the bottom zipper. And finally at the very bottom of the pack is a small compartment that contains a handy and very useful rainfly. No need to buy another! I still would waterproof the rainfly with repellent for extra rain proofing.

The only drawback I see is a lack of molle loops, so as a previous reviewer noted means it is not meant for heavy duty hikes. I still feel it would be nice to have a couple because I like to attach my flip flops and a few rags to the outside of the pack. Having one or two would be very useful.

Overall this is a really good packs for long day hikes or light overnights. 50L gives you plenty of capacity for light backpacking or a heavy duty day hike. Well worth the money, and with the quality of Osprey and their wonderful guarantee, who can go wrong with this?
text_fidelity_b: Osprey Stratos 50 Men's Backpacking Backpack

text_fidelity_a:
LEZYNE MTB Specific Micro Floor Drive Pump Read good reviews of the Lezyne Micro Floor Drive HV on [...] and figured I'd give it a try. My previous hand pump was too tiring on the arms when pumping up 2.2" tires on the trail. I needed a small floor pump version to carry with me in my CamelBak on my mountain bike rides. The pump I received weighed in at 210g. The mounting bracket was another 18g which I won't need. With my previous hand pump I could easily fit 2 fingers on each side of the T shaped handle for more grip. The Micro Floor Drive HV handle is quite small and I can only fit 1 finger on each side of the handle which feels awkward, but since I can now use 2 hands to press down it's not too bad. Overall I'm happy with this product, but wish it was a bit smaller in length and width.

Pros:
+ Feels very solid
+ Very nice screw on Presta AND Schrader valve
+ Can use like a floor pump
+ Made for pumping MTB tires, pumps air fast

Cons:
- Longer and wider than a typical hand pump
- Small T shaped handle
- Somewhat heavy, weight 228g (210g pump + 18g mounting bracket)

UPDATE (11/5/2014)
I've been using this pump for almost 4 years now and have had zero problems pumping tires with Presta and Schrader valves. 100 pumps will get a 26 x 2.0 tire to a comfortable pressure (I estimate just below 30 psi). 120 pumps will yield a very firm tire. The foot peg makes pumping a breeze. I've updated the rating from 4 to 5 stars and added measurements below.

Measurements:
Length: 12 1/8 inches from base to top of hose wrapped around the T-handle
Length: 11 3/4 inches from base to top of T-handle
Width: 63.6 mm (2.5") at base
Width: 45.7 mm (1.8") half way from base with hose touching sides of cylinder
Width: 52.8 mm (2.08") at T-handle including hose on both sides
Depth: 30.3 mm (1.2") at base
Depth: 19.8 mm (0.78") at T-handle

text_fidelity_a:
Mirrycle MTB Bar End Mountain Bicycle Mirror , Black Just installed the Mirrycle bicycle mirror today and took it for a test run.

A few observations and comments.

Agreed, assembly is not entirely easy. As mentioned by numerous reviews, the screws drive hard to the point that you think you’re actually cracking the plastic plus the included Allen wrench requires some strength to turn. But not to worry. Read the instructions and they’ll confirm the hard drive and that you will not crack the plastic. I didn’t try WD40 or any other lubricant so cannot say if that would ease the assembly.

I installed the Mirrycle onto a GT hybrid bicycle and after using a Dremel tool to create an opening in the end of my handle grip I found the handlebar opening accepted the smaller of the two wedges for mounting. I chose to follow the alternative down and under installation mentioned on Amazon reviews which is quite clever and works very well however I believe you may get a better site picture using the “normal” above and to the side installation which would facilitate not having to move your eyes so far from your frontal path to do so. The primary disadvantage to the “normal” up-and-out installation is that the mirror really sticks out there very exposed and if/when you dump your bike or ride close to any shrubs, etc., your mirror will be the early casualty, plus the storage shed where we keep our bikes is small which would necessitate tucking the mirror in upon each return. Do whichever works best for you.

From the lower mounting position I could see both myself and directly behind me but I don’t believe that provides the maximum field of view. On my initial trip I stopped a couple times to adjust the mirror in a similar manner to what you would do with a car, i.e., if you can see part of yourself/your bike in the mirror, tilt it out just a little further until you can’t and that should be about right. Once adjusted properly you only need to tilt your head a tad one way to see either part of yourself directly behind the mirror or a tad the other way to see much more of the road to your direct left.

I was amazed at how solid this mirror rode exhibiting absolutely no jitter or vibration. The large convex shape offered a wide, clear field of view which allowed me not only to see what was coming from behind me but also what was to the near left rear of me as well.

This was only my first day with this product but I’m impressed with the quality and the flexible mounting options it offers.
text_fidelity_b: Mirrycle MTB Bar End Mountain Bicycle Mirror , Black

ALPS Mountaineering Meramac 3-Person Tent I wanted some room to be able to spend time in a tent when it rains. While not as roomy as I hoped after setting it up, it ended up being perfect for a solo car camper. A single size air mattress takes up just about 1/2 the tent. Leaving the other half for keeping some items around, room to change clothes, etc.

I say it ended up being "perfect" because much bigger and it would have been hard too setup by one person. The fabric feels just right, not too thick, not too thin. The zippers worked about as expected on a tent. You have to fiddle a bit at times, but they held up well to my yanking and pulling. I like the dual doors and the screen 'windows' on the doors.

It rained one day and as others have said I stayed perfectly dry. Don't think the over hang of the fly is any kind of vestibule. It's just enough to keep rain out of an open door.

Like most tents you subtract one person from the size . . . this is a roomy tent for one, a good fit for two for sleeping. Two single size air mattresses would be a tight fit in this tent to give some idea of the practical size.

I could go on and on but for the money this was a great purchase and I have zero regrets about buying it. I have no feeling like I should have spent more money on a tent, or should upgrade for my next trip, etc.

I'm not going to take a star off for this since it's not the fault of the tent, but it seems like I got a 'used' tent but it was like brand new. The only way I knew it was used was because A) the box was open and B) some of items had dirt (like the kind of dirt you find in dusty campgrounds) on them. But I figured the dust was from my taking it out of the box/bag, even though I knew the pole ends had not touched the ground yet and they were dirty, but I figured it could have happened, and went on with setting it up. But imagine my surprise when unzipping it for the first time there was a pine needle inside the tent. That was the only debris on the inside, no dirt/dust. It's actually a bit of a mystery since the tent in all other ways appeared brand new and packed well, etc.

The order was filled from Amazon and it was the last one in stock when I ordered. I'm not mad because the tent in all ways performed as a brand new tent. I have had so many good experiences with Amazon that this one little thing is no big deal.
text_fidelity_b: ALPS Mountaineering Meramac 3-Person Tent

Lazer O2 Helmet: White/Red; XL/2XL fits (61-64cm) I just received this from my wife as a Christmas gift. I have gone on 3 rides ranging from 20-60 miles and this helmet is great. A few months ago I went into my favorite local bike shop asking about helmets because I seem to have an unusually large head......yea, a mellon head. Most of the helmets I've tried were too small, too heavy, straps ran weird and uncomfortable, or just plain SQUARE. The Lasor O2 fit like no other helmet I've ever tried. This summer I started useing a "halo" sweat band and I have no problem with the fit, even with my huge mellon head. The unique helmet features a "adjustment dial" that will fine tune the fit to your head with laser percision. This helmet is much lighter than my old Bell I used to wear. You might not notice this on a 10-20 mile ride but if you ride any longer distances you will feel it. During the summer months, I live in Michigan, I try to do one century a month and ...BOY, I can hardly wait to do my first one this year. Another very important feature about this helmet is ....IT LOOKS COOL!! Even my niehbor who likes to make fun of cyclists because of there "pointy hats" said this one looks cool.

Don't look at another helmet. This is the best I've EVER worn. If you cycle a lot, don't hesitate. It's a bit more money but for the serious cyclist it's worth every penny. I try to ride at least 100 mile a week during the good months. If you ride simply with a family or short distances you might want to concider a cheaper model.....unless you have a big fat mellon head like me.
text_fidelity_b: Lazer O2 Helmet: White/Red; XL/2XL fits (61-64cm)
